phase_name: Bracket Postflight Stages 7-8a in the Scope Mutex

objectives.description: Acquire mutex immediately before Stage 7 with POSTFLIGHT_SCOPE_STALE_SEC=30
Export SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD=1 so Stage 7's update-task-status.sh child inherits the guard
Install EXIT trap immediately after successful acquire (first trap in this script)
Release explicitly at close of Stage 8a, clear trap, unset SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD; Stage 8b/9/10 outside
Timeout logs WARNING and continues unserialized (non-blocking)
Bracket comment cites task-lock.md and git-staging-scope.md by name, no task-number citations

notes: Highest-risk phase; tested with extra care per the orchestrator's explicit warnings. Deployed the updated orchestrator-postflight.sh (plus already-deployed Phase 2/3 task-lock.sh and update-task-status.sh) to .claude/scripts/ and ran the REAL script end-to-end against a disposable scratch task (project_number 99999, operation_type=research so do_git_commit=false and Stage 9 is structurally never reached -- confirmed no commit was created, git HEAD unchanged throughout). Findings: (1) the integrated run printed 'Note: an outer holder already owns the specs/.scope-lock mutex (SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD=1 inherited); running as guest, no nested acquire.' during Stage 7 -- direct proof the deadlock-prevention guard fires in the real postflight path, not just in isolation. (2) A background poller confirmed specs/.scope-lock present during the run and absent immediately after. (3) The system was under heavy concurrent load from sibling agent sessions during testing (generate-todo.sh measured at 23ms in Phase 1 was reproducibly ~2.4s during this phase's testing, confirmed independent of my changes via direct re-timing) -- this made raw wall-clock deltas an unreliable regression signal, so the deadlock regression check was instead done as a load-independent A/B comparison: (A) external scope-lock hold + SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD unset -> update-task-status.sh's own nested acquire attempts and waits out the full ~5s contention timeout (8.882s total under current load) before warning and proceeding non-blocking; (B) the SAME external hold + SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD=1 (exactly as Stage 7 sets it) -> guest mode fires immediately, zero mutex-related wait, remaining 2.383s matching ambient system load exactly. This isolates and proves the guard's effect independent of noise. (4) Two concurrent update-task-status.sh runs against two different scratch tasks (99999, 99998) both completed successfully with neither losing the other's state.json write. (5) Verified structurally via grep that the release block precedes both Stage 8b and Stage 9 in file order and neither references scope_token/SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD, confirming the mutex boundary. All scratch state (task rows 99999/99998, scratch task directory, .scope-lock) was cleaned up afterward via targeted jq del() operations on the live, possibly-concurrently-modified state.json (never a wholesale overwrite); task 882's own row and TODO.md/state.json content for all other tasks were verified unaffected.
